title: GAN Fundamentals
interviewAnswer: A GAN trains a generator to fool a discriminator while the discriminator learns to distinguish real from generated samples. This adversarial game can produce sharp images but may be unstable.
why: GAN fundamentals are needed to explain CycleGAN/VQGAN and to compare adversarial training with diffusion/flow matching.
intuition: The generator tries to create samples that look real; the discriminator tries to tell real from generated. Training improves both in a game rather than optimizing one fixed supervised target.
deepDive: The original minimax GAN objective can suffer from saturated gradients and unstable dynamics because generator/discriminator objectives change together. Variants such as non-saturating loss, Wasserstein objectives, gradient penalty, spectral normalization and architectural constraints improve behavior. Mode collapse occurs when the generator covers only part of the data distribution.
workedExample: If a generator produces only one realistic-looking grain pattern regardless of noise input, the discriminator may be fooled locally but diversity is poor—classic mode collapse.
code:
# training alternates conceptually:
# 1) update D on real and detached fake samples
# 2) update G so D scores generated samples as real
commonMistakes: Saying GAN loss values alone directly measure image quality.
Training G and D without controlling detach/update boundaries.
Assuming adversarial realism guarantees semantic or physical correctness.
production: GAN inference can be fast, but training reproducibility and validation are difficult. Store checkpoints/metrics and evaluate diversity plus task-specific correctness, not only discriminator loss.

lab.goal: See the two-player GAN objective with a minimal discriminator score and generator target.
lab.buildIt:
import math
def sigmoid(x): return 1/(1+math.exp(-x))
real_logit=2.0; fake_logit=-1.0
D_real,D_fake=sigmoid(real_logit),sigmoid(fake_logit)
d_loss=-(math.log(D_real)+math.log(1-D_fake))
g_loss=-math.log(D_fake)
print(D_real,D_fake,d_loss,g_loss)
lab.useIt:
# In PyTorch, use BCEWithLogitsLoss rather than applying sigmoid manually.
import torch
loss=torch.nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()(torch.tensor([fake_logit]),torch.ones(1))
print(loss.item())
